messages.subject: Re: Detection history
parts:
Hi,
it looks messy but I believe the issue should be solved easily. The problem is highlighted in red:

dethist_vulpes <- detectionHistory(recordTable = vulpes,
                             camOp = cam_operation,
                             stationCol = "Station",
                             speciesCol = "Species",
                             recordDateTimeCol = "DateTimeOriginal",
                             species = "VTA",
                             occasionLength = 1,
                             day1 = "2018-04-03",
                             datesAsOccasionNames = TRUE,
                             includeEffort = TRUE,
                             scaleEffort = FALSE,
                             timeZone = "Australia/Canberra")

This is a bit of leftover code from the function example. Replace it with the species you are interested in, which would be one of unique(vulpes$Species).

speciesCol = "Species" is correct and replacing speciesCol = "Species" with vulpes$Species will not work. Argument speciesCol is the column name, not the species names themselves, and should have length 1. vulpes$Species on the other hand has as many values as the record table has rows, i.e. length(vulpes$Species) = nrow(vulpes). This is what caused the error message:

Error in checkForSpacesInColumnNames(stationCol = stationCol, setupCol = setupCol,  : 
  this is a bug in 'checkForSpacesInColumnNames'. I'm sorry. Please report it.

Exiftool is innocent in this case. While it is a good idea to avoid spaces in folder and file names, it should usually work. What really messes up things is special characters in folder names.

Please let me know if the error persists.
Best wishes,
Jürgen

sorry, I was not being clear. What you want to do is:

1. find the name of the species as it appears in the species column of your record table, i.e. one of the values returned by unique(vulpes$Species). From the code above I assume you have an entry "Vulpes vulpes".
2. Run detectionHistory with argument species = "Vulpes vulpes".
